events.title: DEC VAX-11/780 announced
events.summary: Digital Equipment Corporation announced the VAX-11/780 on October 25, 1977 — a 32-bit minicomputer that became the benchmark for virtual-memory Unix systems, with first revenue shipments in January 1978.
events.about: VAX machines ran VMS and hosted Unix — universities, labs, and enterprises used them for email, compilers, and time-sharing. The VAX architecture's virtual memory model influenced how operating systems managed address spaces. DEC's install base was where many developers first logged into a multi-user system before PCs and the web.

narrative.whyChosen: The VAX-11/780 defined the 32-bit minicomputer era and DEC's dominance in technical computing.
narrative.whyImportant: It brought affordable virtual memory and timesharing to departments that outgrew PDP-11s.
narrative.problemSolved: Growing software needed larger address spaces and reliable virtual memory beyond 16-bit minis.
